meta.title: File:Ornamental Base and Projecting Wall of Kandariya Mahadev Temple, Khajuraho.jpg
meta.desc: The lower elevation of Kandariya Mahadeva is composed of a richly ornamented jagati and a series of projecting and recessed wall sections. Decorative bands, sculpted figures and geometric motifs continue across the sandstone surface, creating a unified architectural treatment. The monument is one of the most elaborate surviving examples of Chandella-era temple architecture at Khajuraho.

meta.title: File:Carved Mandapa and Towering Shikhara of Kandariya Mahadev Temple, Khajuraho.jpg
meta.desc: The architectural composition of Kandariya Mahadeva consists of axially aligned spaces leading toward the sanctum, with the principal tower rising above it. Its elevated sandstone platform, projecting transepts, ornate halls and clustered spires form a sophisticated example of northern Indian Nagara architecture developed under the Chandella dynasty.

meta.title: File:Clustered Shikharas of Kandariya Mahadeva Temple, Khajuraho.jpg
meta.desc: The principal shikhara of Kandariya Mahadeva rises above the sanctum and is surrounded by a succession of smaller clustered spires. This vertical arrangement is characteristic of the mature Nagara tradition at Khajuraho, where the temple's architectural composition evokes a mountainous form. The monument is constructed primarily of sandstone and dates to the Chandella period.

meta.title: File:Carved Lower Wall and Sculptural Facade of Kandariya Mahadeva Temple, Khajuraho.jpg
meta.desc: Kandariya Mahadeva Temple is an 11th-century Chandella temple dedicated to Shiva and one of the principal monuments of Khajuraho’s Western Group. Built in sandstone, it exemplifies mature Nagara architecture through its elevated jagati, richly carved walls and vertically rising shikhara surrounded by miniature spires. The temple forms part of the UNESCO-listed Khajuraho Group of Monuments.
